q: Density is the ratio of _____ to volume of a substance.
e: Density is the ratio of mass to volume of a substance. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location. Weight: the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force.
Density is a scalar quantity. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. Vector: a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

q: In the density formula, $\rho$ represents a _____ alphabet.
e: In the density formula, $\rho$ represents a Greek alphabet. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in _____.
e: In SI unit, density is expressed in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In CGS unit, density is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or _____.
e: In CGS unit, density is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per millilitre ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$). Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a _____.
e: Mass of an object can be measured using a balance. The physics in this sentence is built around balance.

q: Volume of a substance can be measured using a _____.
e: Volume of a substance can be measured using a measuring cylinder. The physics in this sentence is built around measuring cylinder.

q: Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the _____.
e: Mass of the object does not change, but the volume depends on the temperature. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is.

q: If the volume changes, the _____ will change.
e: If the volume changes, the density will change. Density here means mass per unit volume. Mass: the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: According to Table 4.1, the density of water at $4^{\circ}\text{C}$ is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: According to Table 4.1, the density of water at $4^{\circ}\text{C}$ is 1000 $\text{kg m}^{-3}$. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: According to Table 4.1, the density of mercury is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: According to Table 4.1, the density of mercury is 13600 $\text{kg m}^{-3}$. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: According to Table 4.1, the density of gold is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: According to Table 4.1, the density of gold is 19300 $\text{kg m}^{-3}$. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: The average density of a human body is a little _____ than water density.
e: The average density of a human body is a little less than water density. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.
